parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs one of the most protective documented subnational frameworks with an active hostile national layer that reaches every visitor. Federal border exposure is universal and unavoidable: binary-only passport sex markers, visa adjudication that can treat document discrepancies as permanent fraud ineligibility, entry refusals including a trans-athlete ban, and secondary screening that outs travelers. National facilities, immigration custody, and corrections carry documented severe harms (forced stripping of transition care, abuse in custody). The state/province adds strong operative protections — public-accommodation nondiscrimination since 2014, hate-crime coverage, panic-defence abolition, sanctuary status, healthcare access — and ranks in the safest band with low recorded incidents, though two trans killings in ten weeks are documented without a denominator. Compared with the 0.65 anchors, this case has materially harsher national border/custody exposure than 0.65-A/B but far stronger protective law; compared with 0.75-C, the national entry and custody layer is worse. The worst documented feature sits between tier 2 (national facility/custody regimes) and functioning protective remedies below; a protective state within this parent regime rates around 0.65–0.70.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal passport rules force birth-sex markers; X markers ended; travelers report confiscation and stranding abroad. Visa cable directs refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility on document discrepancy; trans-athlete entry ban; foreign advisories issued about travel here.
entry_documents.protection: Lawsuit challenging passport policy unresolved; no operative federal remedy documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Passport/fraud determinations are federal regardless of protective state law; discrepancy can escalate to investigation and lifetime ineligibility.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections and immigration custody show severe documented abuse: hormone denial, 'conversion' policies, forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans men. State custody placement for trans people is unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented at state level for visitors; federal injunctions have blocked some orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any federal arrest or immigration detention triggers the abusive custody regime regardless of state law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars gender-identity-congruent use of federally funded single-sex facilities; 21+ state/provinces have facility bans, 4 criminal in some circumstances, with at least one arrest and 24-hour men's-ward detention documented. This state/province has no such ban; courts affirmed student facility access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State nondiscrimination law covers public accommodations; gender-neutral county/city ordinances.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Traveler exposure depends on itinerary; federal buildings and ban states within reach of any trip.

care_services.exposure: National hostility to gender-affirming care; public insurance rule proposed barring care under 18; federal subpoenaing of hospitals; visitors with minors face heightened scrutiny if seeking care.
care_services.protection: State sanctuary law and most transgender-friendly healthcare insurance law in the country; access to gender-affirming healthcare protected by 2023 executive order; whether sanctuary protections cover non-residents unsourced.
care_services.interaction: State care access operates beneath federal funding and investigation regimes targeting providers and minors' care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders describe gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', direct prosecution of teachers facilitating transition, list 'radically pro-transgender' ideology among counterterrorism priorities, and reward information leading to arrests; demonization raises outing stakes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime statute covering gender identity; panic-defence abolition; 2020 Supreme Court employment protection remains on paper but targeted by federal order.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing licenses enforcement posture nationally; state police and institutions operate differently.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent traveling with a trans minor faces federal framing of affirming care as child abuse, prosecution directives for facilitators, school investigation orders, records subpoena campaigns, and 27 state/province care bans; federal youth services withdrawn.
minors_guardians.protection: In this state/province, care bans absent, student facility access affirmed, healthcare coverage broad; sanctuary statute aimed partly at families seeking care.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's transition visible to schools/clinics can trigger federal investigation even where state law protects.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Two Black trans women shot dead in the state's largest city within ten weeks (Sep 2026), perpetrators at large; no background-rate denominator to gauge whether this exceeds baseline. State-level incident count otherwise low and in the safest band.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute with gender identity; functioning state institutions; protective-law floor.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw figures without denominators cannot be read as a campaign; documented institutional response thin on these killings.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Whether sanctuary law protects non-resident visitors unsourced; state custody placement unresolved; no per-capita violence data; federal litigation outcomes pending, so operative rules shift with travel timing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State commission on LGBTIQ+ affairs, nondiscrimination enforcement machinery, county bill of rights documented as operating.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Legal-aid FAQ exists for travelers navigating federal document rules; state remedies do not bind federal officers.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Vellmaris, protective national/state law exists and courts eventually function, and local life is broadly safe with occasional friction. But this jurisdiction's national entry regime (fraud findings, refusals, passport confiscation) and documented custody abuse are materially harsher than Vellmaris's single corrective-handling incident, so it sits below 0.65-A.

The federal secondary screening and discretionary refusal resemble Kestrel Isles's variable border screening, but here the exposure extends past the border into facilities, custody and care, and severity includes documented abuse, not just humiliation and delay. This jurisdiction is more protected at state level but more exposed federally; net slightly above 0.55-B.

Meridia's brief-detention border friction with functioning tribunals approximates this state's safe internal environment, but the parent regime here — binary passports, fraud ineligibility threats, custody abuse, counterterror framing — is far more hostile than Meridia's, so this jurisdiction sits clearly below 0.75-C despite equal state protections.

Unlike Vellandra's register, entry refusals here are not universal or automatic, courts have blocked several federal orders, and a functioning protective state exists; the traveler is not met by routine exclusion. Far above the 0.35 band.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a two-layer system: a protective, well-institutionalised state floor (nondiscrimination since 2014, sanctuary status, healthcare access, hate-crime recourse, low recorded incidents) beneath an actively hostile national regime whose document rules, visa fraud doctrine, facility orders, custody practices and threat framing reach every traveler before and regardless of the protective state. Entry-document exposure is universal; custody abuse is severe where federal jurisdiction is triggered; state protections govern most daily-life and facility interactions within the state. The unresolved sanctuary-law scope, pending litigation, and denominator-less local killings temper confidence. Net: clearly safer than the 0.35 and 0.25 bands, below protective-regime 0.75 anchors because federal exposure is documented, operative, and unavoidable at the border.
